transcript.content:
Honestly I'd be surprised if the Moon can be seen right now, but give me your honest estimate anyway.

I'm in Perth, Australia at 2026-07-12 19:25 AWST (UTC+0800) (2026-07-12T11:25:00Z in UTC), at latitude -31.9505 degrees and longitude 115.8605 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is -23.762 degrees and its azimuth is 281.646 degrees, so it is below the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is -51.919 degrees and its azimuth is 275.986 degrees, so it is below the horizon. The Moon is 5.75 percent illuminated, 27.675 degrees from the Sun, and 364757 kilometers away. The sky brightness is night, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Based on the data you provided, my honest estimate is: **No, you will not be able to see the Moon.**

Here is the breakdown of why:

### 1. The Altitude (The "Hard" No)
The most definitive piece of data is the altitude: **-51.919 degrees**. 
In astronomy, an altitude of 0 degrees means the object is exactly on the horizon. A negative number means it is below the horizon. Since the Moon is over 50 degrees below the horizon, it is physically blocked by the curvature of the Earth. You would have to be standing in a very deep canyon or looking through a massive amount of atmosphere (which would still obscure it) to see it.

### 2. The Phase and Brightness
Even if the Moon were just barely peeking above the horizon (say, at -1 or -2 degrees), it would be extremely difficult to see. You noted it is only **5.75% illuminated**. 
*   At this phase (a very thin waxing crescent), the Moon is quite dim.
*   Because it is only 27.6 degrees away from the Sun, it would be located in the same general area of the sky as the Sun. Even if it were above the horizon, the "washout" from the Sun's proximity would make a tiny crescent very hard to distinguish from the surrounding sky.

### 3. The Geometry
The Sun is at -23.7 degrees and the Moon is at -51.9 degrees. This means the Moon is significantly deeper underground (metaphorically speaking) than the Sun is. 

**Verdict:** 
Unless you have a high-powered telescope and are standing on a mountain peak that somehow defies the curvature of the Earth, **the Moon is invisible to you right now.**
